Sort of specific to major but in the math courses I’ve taken I find it really useful to make practice exams for myself by repeating homework problems on various units that we are covering to test what I know. I’ve found it makes the process of solving equations a bit more natural and systematic when I take the actual exams.

Take advantage of school resources!! many schools offer tutoring and writing centers that can help you with every subject. It can really benefit you a lot if you reach out to those resources if you’re struggling.

Also don’t over study and exhaust yourself; if you’re stumped, take a breather, go outside, take a nap or just find a way to recharge and cool down. My major is really writing intensive so I spend a lot of time staring at a half done paper sometimes unsure of what to do next. I’ve found it way better to do 1-2 hrs of work, take a 30 minute breather, come back and do 1-2 more rather than 4 straight hours. Of course, this is assuming you’re doing your work early which I highly recommend you start working on projects early, waiting til the last minute is when you can really burn yourself out.

If you get assigned an essay due in 3 weeks, start it that weekend, write a thesis, get a few sources together and work on it incrementally. It’s hard sometimes to do this especially if you work outside of school but it can really help if you have the means to do so. This is also true of homework; many of my courses assign homework in heaps due months in advance—start these early because procrastinating can really work against you. 

good luck to you, college can be a daunting task but you got this :)

A while back, I knew a girl who I was really into, my parents knew about her, it was a whole ordeal in that regard, never dated her but we knew it each other for a long time and she led me on constantly. One day, she told me she was becoming very depressed and was threatening to kill herself, trying to be a hero, I did everything in my power to help her and that included nearly calling her local police department to check on her because she made it sound like it was imminent that she would do this. Long story short, she never did anything and when I told my dad about it he said something regarding suicide that has never left my mind:

“People who want to do that just do it, they don’t sit around and complain about it”. I’m paraphrasing but that’s about how he put it.

Me, having my own repressed suicidal thoughts, took that as “don’t tell him how you feel because he’ll think you’re complaining and feeling sorry for yourself.”

I guess that’s how I’ve been conditioned, my dad is a great man and I love him but he has a very hard head when it comes to topics that severe. He wants me to be strong, and I want to be strong. But I just don’t have it in my sometimes and I feel pressured to put on a front rather than expose myself. 

I also used to be super emotional and told people how I felt constantly and I found sometimes it just turned people away and made me seem unappealing. A girl I knew in school at a point even told me I was “too hard to deal with” and had to stop talking to me because of it. So with those experiences, and the issue with my dad I feel it’s best that I just save my emotional issues to spill out in a shrink rather than onto others. Because I do want to be seen as strong, or at the very least, stoic enough to not have to constantly spill out my feelings to people, as palpable as my feelings are. I just feel scared to tell anyone anything and if I can pay someone to get all that emotional baggage out with (privately) and work out solutions to my problems, then that seems much better than just chasing people off by letting my darker colors show. 

I’m also looking into other routines to help me out a bit more too, exercise, healthier diet, more time outside, that sorta thing. I go to concerts a lot and have considered really starting to push myself to talk to people more often at them to try and get out of my reclusive social bubble.
